A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 22-page versions of the same RACE research work. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices can be matched, including the renumbered experimental appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original HART detection experiments, rhetorical-relation analysis, ablations, robustness evaluations, and supplementary results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: RACE retains the same extraction, graph initialization, message passing, readout, and joint training objective. Figure 3's revised embedding and pooling notation clarifies the procedure already defined in v1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same four text categories on HART, covering Arxiv, Essay, News, and Writing. The represented generators and evaluation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same twelve baselines, including CoCo, LF-Motifs, SeqXGPT, and the Binoculars and Fast-DetectGPT variants. Comparator membership also remains unchanged within the supplementary comparisons.

E3.justification: The split procedures, partition counts, group-aware evaluation, leave-one-domain-out protocol, metrics, and model configurations are unchanged. Adding percentage units to Table 2's caption clarifies reporting without changing evaluation.

E4.justification: The component ablations, parser replacement, feature-discriminability analysis, text-length analysis, OOD tests, and stricter group-split check retain the same designs and evidence. The Figure 2 corrections concern labeling and reported findings.

E5.justification: Both report RACE's main results across three runs with different seeds as mean and standard deviation, and retain the same uncertainty reporting in the ablation and rhetorical-similarity tables.

E6.justification: Figure 2(a) swaps the Human and LLM legend labels. Section 2.2 changes reported human enrichment from Attribution/Background to Attribution/Temporal, and LLM enrichment from Elaboration/Evaluation/Enablement to Elaboration/Cause, with corresponding corrections after editing. All numerical values in Tables 1–10 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, Z-score calculation, and Equations (1)–(11) are unchanged. Replacing leaf/non-leaf terminology with EDU/relation labels and updating diagram symbols does not alter the mathematical construction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion retain the same four-class detection objective, creator-editor modeling contribution, and low-false-alarm performance claims.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 now interprets LLM relations as greater reliance on local expansion and describes persistence after editing as structural signatures rather than underlying logic. The broad creator-editor interpretation, three stated limitations, and future-work directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix C explicitly provides the ICTMCG/RACE GitHub repository location, supplementing the project-page link already in v1. Hyperparameters, hardware, checkpoint references, and data-processing instructions are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The added IsaNLP citation in the parser-comparison paragraph refers to Chistova (2024), already cited and discussed in v1.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and terminology edits, reformats the baseline discussion, and adds Juan Cao as a corresponding author. Experimental appendices B/C become A/B, cross-references are updated, and a short reproducibility section is added.

P2.justification: Figure 2's creator legend and caption are corrected. Figure 3 updates token-span, mean-pooling, type-embedding, and root-readout labels. Table 2's caption adds percentage units and Table 6's caption is shortened; the overall display structure remains stable.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves the mismatch between Figure 2's creator labels, plotted patterns, and discussion, clarifies Figure 3 against the existing equations, and adds explicit code access information. These targeted corrections improve internal consistency and reproducibility documentation. The experimental evidence and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
